author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Separate PS2 motion ghosting from deinterlacing and upscaling artifacts
summary: Record motion at native resolution, compare fields and static frames, disable post-processing, test deinterlacing independently, and preserve intentional trails while removing duplicated character edges introduced by the output path.
heroAlt: PCSX2 before-fix capture illustrating a duplicated or offset game image

blocks.text: Determine whether the trail exists in time or in one frame

Intentional motion blur follows movement across frames; a field-combination error often creates a comb or doubled edge inside one output frame; an upscaling artifact can create a fixed offset copy even while the camera is still. Record a slow horizontal camera pan and a motionless character at the same location. Inspect individual captured frames as well as playback. That distinction decides whether to test deinterlacing, resolution, or a title-specific framebuffer correction.
Do not remove every trail by sharpening or forcing a random deinterlacing mode. Some games deliberately accumulate previous frames, and destroying that pass can also remove bloom or depth effects.
Capture motion and stillness under one profile

items: A reproducible camera pan with a high-contrast character edge.
A stationary pause of several seconds in the same scene.
Screen recording at the device's native refresh without social-media recompression.
Post-processing, texture packs, and display motion smoothing disabled.
Recorded deinterlacing mode, aspect ratio, and internal resolution.

blocks.text: Isolate the source of the duplicate edge

items: 1. Cold-boot at native internal resolution and record the pan plus the stationary hold.
2. Step through frames: note whether the copy alternates by field, fades over time, or remains at a constant pixel offset.
3. Leave resolution unchanged and cycle only supported deinterlacing choices, returning to the checkpoint for each clip.
4. Choose the mode that stabilizes moving edges without making the entire image bob or soften excessively.
5. If the stationary frame still has an offset copy, restore Automatic deinterlacing and disable post-processing stages one by one.
6. If native output is clean, increase internal resolution one step and repeat the exact camera path.
7. When a problem begins only above native, consult a documented title-specific upscaling correction rather than borrowing offsets from another game.
8. Verify gameplay, FMV, menus, and a second camera speed before keeping the result.

blocks.text: Interlaced PS2 output stores temporal information in fields, so a still screenshot alone can misrepresent the failure. Emulator post-effects can also reuse prior framebuffer content on purpose. Native-resolution evidence removes sampling changes from the first branch; motion clips reveal cadence; a stationary hold reveals fixed copies. Each branch has a different remedy and should be tested without combining settings.
A good result keeps intentional presentation while eliminating the unintended duplicate contour.

items: Walking and camera pans show stable silhouettes without comb teeth.
A motionless character does not retain a displaced copy.
Deliberate blur, bloom, and depth-of-field still appear where the game uses them.
FMV playback has correct cadence and no new bobbing.
The selected mode survives a cold boot and device rotation or display reconnect.

blocks.text: Ghosting clues that need another branch

items: The duplicate appears in an original-console reference: treat it as game presentation.
Only the external television shows trails: disable its motion interpolation and inspect panel response.
The copy begins after loading a save state: reproduce from an in-game save.
Every renderer shows a corrupt fixed offset at native output: collect a rendering report instead of tuning further.

blocks.text: Set deinterlacing to Automatic, remove the tested post-processing stage and upscaling offset, return to native resolution, and replay the baseline clip. Keep original lossless frames with settings so later driver or emulator changes can be compared honestly.

Photographing a screen mixes display persistence, rolling shutter, refresh mismatch, and camera exposure. Use the emulator's direct capture for frame evidence; use a camera only when documenting an external display-chain problem.
